bean.name: KeycloakSecurityPolicy
bean.title: Keycloak Security Policy
bean.description: An authorization policy that validates the caller's Keycloak access token and checks its roles and permissions before the part of the route it guards runs. A caller that fails is denied with CamelAuthorizationException.

serverUrl.description: The base URL of the Keycloak server, for example http://localhost:8080.

realm.description: The Keycloak realm the tokens are issued in.

clientId.description: The client id of this application in the realm.

clientSecret.label: security
clientSecret.description: The client secret, for a confidential client.

username.label: security
username.description: The user to sign in as when useResourceOwnerPasswordCredentials is enabled.

requiredRoles.description: Comma-separated list of the roles the caller must have, for example admin,user. Whether it needs all of them or any one is set by allRolesRequired.

requiredPermissions.description: Comma-separated list of the permissions the caller must have, for example read:documents,write:documents. Whether it needs all of them or any one is set by allPermissionsRequired.

allRolesRequired.description: Whether the caller must have all the required roles, rather than any one of them.

allPermissionsRequired.description: Whether the caller must have all the required permissions, rather than any one of them.

useResourceOwnerPasswordCredentials.label: security
useResourceOwnerPasswordCredentials.description: Whether the policy's Keycloak client signs in with username and password, the resource owner password credentials grant, rather than with clientId and clientSecret.

publicKey.label: security
publicKey.description: The public key to verify token signatures with. Used only when autoFetchPublicKey is false, which it is not by default.

useTokenIntrospection.label: security
useTokenIntrospection.description: Whether to validate tokens with Keycloak's token introspection endpoint rather than by parsing the JWT locally, which detects a token revoked before it expires.

introspectionCacheEnabled.label: advanced
introspectionCacheEnabled.description: Whether to cache token introspection results, to reduce the calls to Keycloak.

introspectionCacheTtl.label: advanced
introspectionCacheTtl.description: How long a cached introspection result is kept, in seconds, given as a plain number rather than a time pattern such as 5m.

validateTokenBinding.label: security
validateTokenBinding.description: Whether a token from a header must match the token bound to the session, which prevents session fixation.

allowTokenFromHeader.label: security
allowTokenFromHeader.description: Whether the token may come from a message header. Disable it where the route sets the token itself, so a caller cannot inject one through a header.

preferPropertyOverHeader.label: security
preferPropertyOverHeader.description: Whether a token in an exchange property wins over one in a header, which prevents a header from overriding the token the route established.

validateIssuer.label: security
validateIssuer.description: Whether a token must have been issued by the configured serverUrl and realm, which prevents cross-realm token injection.

autoFetchPublicKey.label: security
autoFetchPublicKey.description: Whether to fetch the keys that verify token signatures from the realm's JWKS endpoint, and cache them.

jwksRefreshInterval.label: advanced
jwksRefreshInterval.description: How often the cached JWKS keys are refreshed, in seconds, given as a plain number rather than a time pattern such as 5m.

minJwksRefreshInterval.label: advanced
minJwksRefreshInterval.description: The minimum time between two JWKS refreshes triggered by an unknown key id, which rate-limits the calls to Keycloak, in seconds, given as a plain number rather than a time pattern such as 5m.

expectedAudience.label: security
expectedAudience.description: Comma-separated list of audiences a token must all carry in its aud claim, so that a token issued for another client of the realm is rejected.

expectedTokenTypes.label: security
expectedTokenTypes.description: Comma-separated list of the accepted token types (typ claim), for example Bearer, so that an ID or refresh token is not accepted where an access token is expected.

expectedAuthorizedParty.label: security
expectedAuthorizedParty.description: The client a token must have been issued for (azp claim).
